# Atlas {#sec-app-atlas}

## Overview

The **Atlas** ([marinesensitivity.org/atlas](https://marinesensitivity.org/atlas/)) is a third,
newer way to explore the MST: **one static web app**, built with Svelte and MapLibre, that runs
entirely in the browser. Where the [Scores](scores.qmd) and [Species](species.qmd) Shiny apps are
server-rendered R processes, the Atlas ships as plain HTML/JS/CSS with no server component at
all — every score, click, flower plot and report is computed client-side, in-browser, by a DuckDB
instance compiled to WebAssembly (DuckDB-WASM) that queries the release's own published Parquet
tables directly over HTTPS. The same static build runs unmodified at
`https://marinesensitivity.org/atlas/` (public releases) and at
`https://preview.marinesensitivity.org/{ver}/atlas/` (the signed-in reviewer host for a
`restricted` pre-release, @sec-app-scores's "one application, every release" idea applied to a
different runtime).

::: {.callout-note}
## The version is still data, not a code fork

Exactly as with Scores and Species, there is one Atlas checkout for every release. On the public
host the release is a query parameter (`?ver=v7`), resolved client-side against the published
`versions.json`; defaulting to the promoted release when the parameter is absent. On the preview
host — because Cloudflare Access scopes its reviewer policies by URL **path**, never by query — the
release is the path itself (`/v9/atlas/`), matching the pattern `/v9/scores/` and `/v9/species/`
already use there. A version the current host is not allowed to show (a restricted release
requested on the public host, or an unrecognized `?ver=`) opens the release picker with a link to
"Continue on the preview host" rather than silently falling back to another version's data.
:::

The Atlas combines what the two Shiny apps do separately — mapping composite scores, mapping
individual species distributions — with a capability neither has: **Places**, a tool for drawing,
typing, or uploading your own area of interest (a lease block, a survey footprint, a project
boundary) and getting the same scores and species tables the built-in Program Areas get, then
sharing the exact area and view through the URL and exporting a report. @sec-atlas-places below
covers Places in detail, including the byte-level shape of the codec that carries a drawn shape in
a link.

@fig-atlas-map shows the default Scores view: the 0.05° cell grid colored by a composite
sensitivity score across U.S. waters, dark theme (the app's default), with the tool rail on the
left and the release's own attribution in the lower-right corner.

![The Atlas, Scores lens, default view (desktop, dark theme). that floats over the map (left, right or bottom); on a phone the identical five tools sit in a
labelled **bottom tab bar** — never under a sheet, so the tools stay reachable at every sheet
height — and the panel becomes a **bottom sheet** with three heights (peek, half, full) instead of
a floating card. @fig-atlas-phone-map shows the phone layout: the top bar shrinks to the mark,
release chip, lens switch and theme toggle, with search, Share, Report, Help, About and Feedback
folded into a **⋯ (more) menu** (@fig-atlas-phone-more).

![The phone's ⋯ (more) menu, reached from the top bar, holding the controls a wide viewport shows directly: Share, Report, Feedback, About this release, Take a tour, Docs.](/images/atlas/phone-more-menu.png){#fig-atlas-phone-more}

## Getting around

**The top bar**, left to right: the MST mark and title; a **release chip** that opens the version
picker (every published release, with restricted rows offering "Continue on the preview host" and
retired rows offering "Switch"); a **Scores | Species lens switch**; a **search field** (species and
places — desktop only, folded into the phone's search behavior); then, right-aligned, **Share**
(copies the current view as a link and announces what it carries), **Report** (opens the report
builder for whatever is currently selected), a **(?) Help** menu (Take a tour, a keyboard-shortcut
reference, and a link to this documentation book), the **About / Feedback / ⋯** control group, and a
sun/moon **theme toggle**.

**The tool rail** is five controls, always in the same order, on every viewport:
**Layers · Places · Flower plot · Table · Report**. In the Species lens the Flower control fades in
place — a flower plot has no meaning for a single species — but it is never removed, and its
tooltip says why ("Flower plot — Scores only") rather than just disappearing.

**The panel** that a rail tool opens is one dockable surface, not a fixed sidebar:

- **Dock** left, right or bottom (a horizontal drawer), from a control in its header.
- **Resize** by dragging its map-facing edge (320–720 px), or with arrow keys on the same handle.
- **Maximize** to the whole stage — a backdrop appears, focus is trapped inside while maximized,
  and the map keeps rendering underneath — or **collapse** to a small labelled pill at the panel's
  edge; clicking any rail tool re-opens a collapsed panel to that tool.
- Its dock/size/collapsed state is **chrome, remembered per viewport size** (browser
  `localStorage`), never written into the shareable URL — only the view state the URL does carry
  (@sec-atlas-place-links) travels with a shared link.

On a phone the same panel becomes the bottom **sheet**, with three detents — peek (its header
only), half (the default) and full — instead of dock/resize/maximize.

A floating **legend chip** tracks the current layer's color ramp; on a phone it floats above the
sheet at peek/half and moves inline inside the sheet at full height, so it never sits over the
sheet's own header controls.

## Scores lens {#sec-atlas-scores}

The Scores lens is the Atlas's equivalent of the [Scores app](scores.qmd): the composite,
extinction-risk-weighted score for every 0.05° cell (or, aggregated, every Program Area) of U.S.
waters. Opening **Layers** (@fig-atlas-layers) shows the one row every lens shares — **Data**,
expandable into that lens's own controls (study area, spatial unit, the score layer, color
palette) — plus the rest of the **layer stack**: outlines/labels, a Program-Area/ecoregion boundary
group, and the basemap's own sub-layers (land & water, bathymetry — present but empty until a
relief layer is published, boundaries, roads & buildings, place labels). Every row in the stack
can be shown/hidden, given an opacity, and **moved up or down** relative to the others — so, for
example, place labels can be pulled above a semi-transparent score raster, or below it.

![The Layers panel: the Data row (study area, spatial unit, layer, palette) expanded above the rest of the stack — outlines, basemap sub-layers — each with a visibility toggle, an opacity slider and move-up/move-down controls.](/images/atlas/desktop-layers.png){#fig-atlas-layers}

Clicking a cell or a Program Area on the map selects it: the URL gains a `sel=cell:<id>` or
`sel=zone:<unit>:<key>` token, and the **Flower plot** and **Table** tools (@sec-atlas-flower-table)
both then describe that selection. Spatial units can be switched between raster cells and Program
Areas from the Data row; four palettes are available (Spectral is the default and the one every
release publishes legend stops for today).

## Species lens

Switching the lens switch to **Species** turns the top-bar search into a species picker (common or
scientific name, with an "Only species in US waters" checkbox), and the panel becomes the species
**card**: the merged model as a filled pill, plus one pill per contributing input dataset the taxon
carries (AquaMaps, BirdLife, IUCN range, critical habitat, …), colored green for the merged model
and orange for each input. An input this release published **no surface** for renders as a
**struck-through, non-interactive pill** — never simply omitted — so a viewer can see what feeds
the model even when this particular release cannot draw it.

Two toggles sit beside the pills: a **representation** toggle — "Original" (the source SDM at its
native resolution) vs. "Interpolated" (resampled to the 0.05° scoring grid), or, for a dataset
that is *delivered* already on that grid (AquaX, from v9 onward), "Delivered" vs. "As ingested" —
mirroring the same native-vs-model comparison the [Species app](species.qmd) offers. Clicking
anywhere on the map returns that cell's modelled value; the legend under the map is titled with the
species' scientific name and its 1–100 range.

![The Species lens' card for the leatherback turtle (*Dermochelys coriacea*): the merged model (six inputs) with five inputs struck through — published for this taxon's merge but not, in this release, as their own drawable surface — beside the species' ESA/IUCN/WoRMS panel.](/images/atlas/desktop-species.png){#fig-atlas-species}

## Places {#sec-atlas-places}

**Places** is the tool the two Shiny apps do not have: any area you outline, not only the built-in
Program Areas, gets the same scores and species results. The empty state spells out every way in:
"Turn on pick mode and click a Program Area, draw a shape, enter coordinates, or drop a file on the
map."

- **Pick a Program Area** two ways: **pick mode** (a toggle; click a Program Area on the map, or
  Ctrl/Cmd-click or long-press to add more than one), or the panel's own **Program Area chooser** —
  a full-name-sorted picker ("St. George Basin (GEB)", not the bare key) that needs no pointer and
  works on a phone, where clicking the map is impractical.
- **Draw** a Polygon, Rectangle or Circle directly on the map (click points, close a polygon on its
  first vertex; a rectangle or circle is a drag). A drawn shape's corners stay draggable afterward,
  and the map outline for a drawn place is magenta.
- **Enter coordinates** — the keyboard/screen-reader alternative to drawing, in a modal dialog
  (@fig-atlas-coords): a bounding box (`xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax`), a list of `lon, lat` vertices one
  per line (three or more), or pasted WKT/GeoJSON. Every refusal (malformed input, too few points, a
  self-intersecting ring) is shown **verbatim** — what went wrong, why, and how to fix it — never a
  bare "invalid input."
- **Upload a file**, either through the picker or by dropping it anywhere on the map
  (@fig-atlas-places below shows the drop zone). The exact accepted-format line, as the app itself
  states it: *"GeoJSON, zipped shapefile, KML, GPX, FlatGeobuf, WKT or GeoPackage, up to 10 MB."*
  (`MAX_FILE_MB = 10` in `src/places/UploadPanel.svelte`.) A file with several shapes prompts a
  choice — keep them as separate places, or merge into one — and a GeoPackage additionally asks
  consent before its one-time fetch, naming the size and the third-party host, because reading one
  needs a separate ~22 MB DuckDB `spatial` extension the app does not otherwise load.

![The Places panel: pick mode, the Program Area chooser, draw tools (Polygon/Rectangle/Circle), "Enter coordinates," and the upload drop zone, above the current place list.](/images/atlas/desktop-places.png){#fig-atlas-places}

![The "Enter coordinates" dialog: a bounding box, a vertex list, or pasted WKT/GeoJSON, with the same verbatim what/why/fix refusal format the upload path uses.](/images/atlas/desktop-coordinate-dialog.png){#fig-atlas-coords}

Each place in the list shows its area, once analyzed its data coverage percentage and composite
score, and per-row actions (rename, zoom to, duplicate, delete). Selecting a place expands its
**results**: a note on what fraction of the place falls inside the U.S. study area ("*N*% of this
place is inside the US study area (*a* of *b* cells)"), a flower plot, a table of component scores,
and — loaded on request, batched over the place's cells — a species table. The panel's footer holds
**Share**, **Download places** (GeoJSON) and **Report**, each disabled until at least one place
exists.

## How places are stored in the link {#sec-atlas-place-links}

A place never lives on a server: it is encoded directly into the URL, so that opening a shared
link reproduces the sender's exact area — this is also why **every analysis runs on the *decoded*
geometry**, never the geometry as drawn, so a place and the numbers describing it can never diverge
between sender and recipient.

Places live in the URL **fragment** (`#pl=`, never the query string, because a fragment is never
sent to a server or a referrer), one place per `~`-separated token:

```
#pl=z.pa.GAA~g1.Monterey%20box.EAECDMSNAdcC...
```

- **`z.<set>.<key>[,<key>...]`** — a reference to a *built-in* zone (`pa` Program Area, `pl`
  Planning Area, `er` ecoregion, `sr` subregion) by key; the geometry itself comes from the
  release's own PMTiles, so the link carries only a few bytes.
- **`g1.<name>.<base64url bytes>`** — a drawn, typed or uploaded polygon, carried inline. `g1` is a
  small hand-rolled binary codec, not GeoJSON-in-base64: each ring is quantized to a fixed
  precision (3 decimal digits, about 110 m — 4 digits for a place under half a degree across),
  delta-encoded vertex-to-vertex as zigzag varints, and base64url-encoded with **no general-purpose
  compression** — the format is already dense, and (per the codec's own source comments) a
  compressed stream would have no straightforward decoder to give the sibling `msens` R package,
  which the design intends to read the identical tokens.[^atlas-g1-r] Longitudes are stored
  **unwrapped**, so a place that crosses the antimeridian round-trips without an antimeridian
  special case.
- **`u.<name>.<8-hex-digit digest>`** — the fallback for a place too large to carry at all: only
  its name and an 8-character SHA-256 digest travel in the link, and the recipient is prompted to
  re-upload or re-draw it.

[^atlas-g1-r]: Not independently verified in this book: at the time of writing the `msens` R
package's own repository does not yet contain a decoder for the `g1` format, although the atlas
source's own test fixture (`tests/fixtures/place_codec.json`) is written to be shared byte-for-byte
with an `msens inst/fixtures/place_codec.json` twin once one exists.

**The URL has a length budget**, applied automatically whenever a place is added, shared or
reported: up to **2,000 characters silently**, up to **8,000 characters with a "long link" note**,
and beyond that a Douglas-Peucker simplification ladder — coarsening at 0.001°, doubling each rung
to 0.002°, 0.004°, 0.008° and 0.016° — where **a rung is accepted only if it changes the place's
area by no more than 1% and leaves every ring simple** (no self-intersections); a rung that would
violate either check is rejected and the next-coarser one is tried instead. If no rung fits the
8,000-character budget even at the coarsest tolerance, the place falls back to the `u.` digest form
described above, and the Share dialog's practical advice is to **download the place as GeoJSON**
and send that alongside the link instead. In practice this means: a simple lease-block rectangle or
a hand-drawn polygon of modest complexity always survives in the link; a highly detailed uploaded
boundary (thousands of vertices) may be silently simplified by a fraction of a percent of its area,
and a truly enormous shapefile will end up as a name-only reference that has to be re-attached.

The **Share** dialog (opened from Places' footer or the top bar) states in one sentence what the
copied link actually carries — *"This link carries release v7, the scores lens, the current map
view, 3 places. Link length: 1,842 characters."* — and, if simplification had to run to fit the
budget, shows the before/after vertex count and area change and requires the numbers on screen to
already reflect the simplified geometry before the link can be copied, so the copied link and the
displayed results can never disagree with each other.

![The Share dialog for a Program Area place: a one-sentence summary of everything the link carries (release, lens, camera, place count) and the link's exact character length — the same dialog a drawn, typed or uploaded place opens.](/images/atlas/desktop-share-dialog.png){#fig-atlas-share}

The rest of the view is carried the same URL-is-the-state way, in the query string rather than the
hash: `ver` (release), `lens` (`scores`/`species`), `lyr`/`sp` (the active layer or species), `unit`
(cell vs. a zone key), `area` (a study-area camera preset), `map` (an explicit camera —
`lon,lat,zoom[,bearing,pitch]`), `pal` (palette), `sel` (the clicked cell or zone), `layers` (the
layer-stack deltas described in @sec-atlas-scores), `theme` and `tour`. Every field is written only
when it differs from its default, so a plain `https://marinesensitivity.org/atlas/` link is never
cluttered by state nobody changed; an unrecognized or malformed value is dropped back to its
default rather than throwing.

## Flower plot and Table {#sec-atlas-flower-table}

**Flower plot**, once a cell, Program Area or Place is selected, shows the same kind of flower the
[Scores app](scores.qmd) draws: one annular petal per species category, its outer radius scaled to
that category's rescaled score, drawn from a shared inner hub that carries the weighted center
value. Tapping or hovering a petal shows its category and value; the same values also list below
the plot as plain text, for a screen reader or a reader who wants the numbers without decoding the
geometry.

![The Flower plot for a clicked cell in the Gulf of Mexico: one annular petal per species category around a centre value, with the component table (and the map popup carrying the same combined-score sentence) below it.](/images/atlas/desktop-flower.png){#fig-atlas-flower}

**Table** opens three tabs on the same panel: a sortable **species table** (scientific/common name,
category, ESA/IUCN/MMPA/MBTA flags, extinction-risk score, model key), a **zones table** (every
Program Area ranked by its composite score, with a "report on selected" action once some are
ticked), and a **composition** treemap (species contribution to the current selection's score, one
level). On a phone the species and zones tables open with a compact default column set and a
**Columns** control to add or remove columns — the choice persists for the session — while both
tables get sticky header/identifying columns and horizontal scrolling that never spills outside the
panel. Every table has a **CSV download**.

![The Table tool's species tab for a clicked cell: sortable, filterable columns (Category, Taxon, Scientific name, Common name, …), with Zones and Composition as the other two tabs.](/images/atlas/desktop-table.png){#fig-atlas-table}

## Report

**Report** builds a self-contained document for whatever places are currently selected —
opened either from the top bar, a rail tool, or a place's own row — and renders progressively, one
section as its data arrives, rather than waiting for everything at once:

- a **header band** with the MST mark, release chip, generation timestamp, the report's own
  permalink and a **QR code** of that permalink (so a printed copy can lead back to the live one);
- an **introduction**, restating what was selected;
- a static **map** snapshot of the selected place(s);
- one **flower plot** per place;
- a **Table of Scores** — every place's component scores and overall score, with footnotes grouped
  one per area for any component whose data coverage falls under the release's coverage floor;
- a **Summary of Species** per place (a category × count cross-tab, plus the top 20 by score);
- **Sources and Method**, with the release's own citations;
- a **Provenance** section: release id, status/access, generation time, the app's build SHA, the
  DuckDB-WASM version, which tables were actually read, and the SQL that actually ran (the same
  query templates `sql/` shares with the `msens` R package) — so the report documents exactly how
  its own numbers were produced, not just what they are.

![The report document: header band with QR permalink, map, flower plot, Table of Scores, species summary and provenance, generated in-browser from the same link that selected the place.](/images/atlas/desktop-report.png){#fig-atlas-report}

Four ways to take the report with you, all built client-side with no server round trip:

- **Print** — calls the browser's own print dialog once; the printed layout is print-media-aware
  (roughly five U.S. Letter pages for a typical report).
- **Download HTML** — one self-contained file (inline CSS, inline SVGs, the map and flower as
  embedded PNG data URIs), openable completely offline.
- **Data package (ZIP)** — `README.md`, `CITATION.md`, `provenance.json`, `places.geojson`, and a
  `scores_*.csv`/`species_*.csv` pair per place, at full numeric precision.
- **Word document (.docx)** — the same Table of Scores, species summary and provenance as coded
  Word styles (no reference template), plus the map and a rasterized flower per place as embedded
  images.

Because the report is derived entirely from the URL, re-opening the exact link it prints in its
header band reproduces the same document — the report *is* reproducible in the same sense the rest
of the MST pipeline is (@sec-apps).

## Accessibility and performance notes

The Atlas ships a written [WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessibility conformance note](https://github.com/MarineSensitivity/atlas/blob/main/docs/accessibility.md) and
a [performance budget report](https://github.com/MarineSensitivity/atlas/blob/main/docs/performance.md) in its own repository; both are living documents
scoped to what is actually automated-tested, not a blanket claim. A few figures worth carrying into
this book:

- **Keyboard.** Every rail tool, panel control (dock/resize/maximize/collapse), layer-stack row and
  dialog is reachable and operable from the keyboard alone; the panel traps focus while maximized
  and restores it correctly on Esc; skip links jump past the map to the tool rail; the map itself
  exposes its data as a text equivalent ("Every zone's score is also in the Zones table, under the
  Table tool") since a rendered raster has no accessible text content of its own.
- **Screen readers.** One shared, polite ARIA live region announces state changes (pick mode
  on/off, a place added, a link copied, a layer moved); every meaningful state (pressed, expanded,
  disabled) is exposed through ARIA attributes, never color alone.
- **First paint.** The critical-path JavaScript is held to a **450 KB gzip** budget (measured
  ~417 KB) plus a **150 KB** budget for the MapLibre runtime worker (~140 KB measured), combining to
  a **600 KB "before first interaction"** ceiling — everything else (drawing tools, the report
  builder, DOCX/ZIP export, the feedback screenshot tool) loads lazily, on demand, well after that.
  A separate timing gate asserts the species lens paints its first data pixel within **2.5 s** on a
  laptop and **4 s** on CI's shared runners (median of repeated cold loads).

## Feedback and versions

**Feedback** (the top bar's control, or the phone's ⋯ menu) opens a dialog rather than jumping
straight to an external site: a kind (bug / idea / question / data), a short description, an
optional email, a client-captured screenshot the reporter can annotate (arrow, circle, rectangle,
pen, text), and a privacy checkbox — **"include my current view link" is off by default**, so a
drawn place's geometry never leaves the device unless the reporter explicitly opts in. It posts to
the project's feedback endpoint, or falls back to a prefilled GitHub issue if that post fails.

**Versions** follow the same public/restricted split described in the
[Releases](../releases.qmd) chapter: a `public`
release opens directly at `https://marinesensitivity.org/atlas/?ver={ver}`; a `restricted`
pre-release under review is offered only as a link to
`https://preview.marinesensitivity.org/{ver}/atlas/`, behind the same Cloudflare Access gate that
protects the preview Scores and Species apps. Opening this book's own release picker inside the
Atlas (the top-bar release chip) is the fastest way to see which releases exist and which one is
promoted, without leaving the app.

![The release picker ("Data release"), opened from the top-bar chip: every published release, its status and date, `restricted` pre-releases offering "Continue on the preview host," and `retired` releases offering "Switch."](/images/atlas/desktop-version-picker.png){#fig-atlas-versions}

::: {.callout-note}
## A note on this section's links

Unlike the Scores and Species pages, the links above are written out directly rather than built
with `doc_app_url()`: that helper's URL shape (`https://app.marinesensitivity.org/{ver}/{app}/`)
does not fit the Atlas, which lives on a different host (`marinesensitivity.org`, not
`app.marinesensitivity.org`) and — on the public host — resolves its release from a query
parameter rather than a path segment. Extending `doc_app_url()` to cover this correctly would be
more than a one-line addition, so this page hard-codes the URLs instead.
:::

## Source Code

[`atlas`](https://github.com/MarineSensitivity/atlas) on its own `main` branch — one static build
for every release, the same "one checkout, not one per version" convention the [Scores](scores.qmd)
and [Species](species.qmd) apps follow. `sql/` holds the DuckDB-WASM query templates that are meant
to be the browser-side twin of the equivalent `msens` R functions; `docs/` in that repository holds
its own design spec, usability walkthroughs, and the accessibility/performance notes cited above.
